To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the recombinant nucleoprotein (NP) of the hantavirus strain 76- 118, a prototype strain of hantavirus in China, was expressed in prokaryotes and its biological activity was confirmed by an ELISA for detection of a set of MAbs.
the expressed recombinant NP of Hantaan Virus (HTNV) can be used for detection of antibodies to HTNV and that the N-terminal of NP is a potential antigenic region.
the expressed complete NP of Hantaan strain 76- 118 has a similar function as authentic viral NP, and the region 1-37 in the N- terminus of NP might be an important antigenic domain of Hantaan NP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the antigenic sites and epitopes of the HTNV NP, which is useful for the development of a diagnostic kit and vaccine against hantavirus.
a novel approach to the antigenic characterization of the expressed complete and different partial recombinant NPs of HTNV by using MAbs.
the expression of recombinant HTNV NP and the antigenic analysis of its epitopes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expressed recombinant NP and truncated N-terminal NPs could be used as a candidate antigen for the development of an immunodiagnostic kit for HTNV infection, and the expressed recombinants could be applied for further studies of hantavirus infection.

the expressed complete and different partial truncated recombinant NP of hantaviruses are useful for the development of a sensitive and specific serological assay for the diagnosis of hantavirus infection and the evaluation of the protective immunity of the hantavirus vaccine.
the recombinant whole and truncated HTNV NPs could be used as diagnostic antigens for the detection of anti-HTNV antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expressed complete or partial HTNV NPs are useful as antigens for the detection of hantavirus-specific antibodies, which will be helpful for the study of hantavirus.

the expressed complete and truncated NPs could be used to detect hantavirus infection in humans and animals, and the expressed NPs would be a potential candidate for a vaccine against hantavirus infection.
the expressed recombinant NP of HTNV was a good antigen for detecting antibodies against HTNV in human sera and that it was a good antigenic target for the production of MAbs against HTNV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recombinant truncated HTNV NP could be a useful tool for seroepidemiological studies, and it may be a good candidate for a subunit vaccine against HTNV infection.
we have developed a new approach to produce recombinant NP protein of HTNV, and we have also identified the antigenic sites of NP protein.
the recombinant HTNV NPs can be produced in large quantities in a short time.
